title: L13 · Muscle Tissue
subtitle: Muscle types, fiber structure, myofilaments, sarcomere, wrappings

lines.text: Myo, sarco and mys all mean muscle.
**Contractility** is the power to shorten. No other tissue can do it.
**Excitability** is responding to a stimulus.
**Extensibility** is being stretched.
**Elasticity** is recoiling back to resting length.
**Skeletal** muscle is voluntary. Long cylinders, many nuclei, striated.
**Cardiac** muscle is only in the heart. Involuntary, branched, striated, usually one nucleus.
**Smooth** muscle lines hollow organs. Involuntary, spindle shaped, one nucleus, no striations.
Only smooth muscle can divide.
Skeletal muscle is 30 to 40 percent of body mass.
The **origin** doesn't move. It's usually proximal.
The **insertion** moves. It's usually distal.
Contraction pulls the insertion toward the origin.
Skeletal muscle moves the body, holds posture, stabilizes joints and makes heat.
Only cardiac muscle has **intercalated discs**.
They hold **desmosomes**, which resist stress.
And **gap junctions**, which pass ions between cells.
Those are the junctions from Lecture 5.
**Visceral** smooth muscle is common. It lines hollow organs.
It usually has an inner circular and an outer longitudinal layer.
The stomach and uterus add an oblique layer.
**Multi-unit** smooth muscle is rare. The iris and the arrector pili.
A skeletal muscle cell is a muscle fiber.
Its membrane is the **sarcolemma**. Its cytoplasm is the **sarcoplasm**.
**T-tubules** dive inward and carry the signal deep into the cell.
The **sarcoplasmic reticulum** stores calcium and releases it on demand.
Its terminal cisternae are calcium reservoirs next to the T-tubules.
Myofibrils fill 80 percent of the fiber.
**Actin** is the thin filament. It has myosin-binding sites.
**Tropomyosin** covers those sites.
**Troponin** sits on tropomyosin. It has a binding site for calcium.
**Myosin** is the thick filament. Its heads reach out to grab actin.
Myofilaments make myofibrils. Myofibrils make fibers.
The **sarcomere** is the smallest unit that can contract.
**Z-discs** mark its ends and anchor the thin filaments.
The **I band** is thin filament only. It's light.
The **A band** is the full thick filament. It's dark, and it never changes length.
The **H zone** is thick filament only, in the middle.
The **M line** holds the thick filaments in line.
Myosin uses **ATP** to walk along actin.
Each grip is a **cross bridge**.
The thin filaments slide toward the center. The sarcomere shortens.
The I band and H zone disappear at full contraction.
It keeps going as long as **calcium** is present.
Three connective tissue layers wrap skeletal muscle.
**Endomysium** wraps one fiber. Paper around a straw.
**Perimysium** wraps a bundle, a fascicle. A box of straws.
**Epimysium** wraps the whole muscle. A shipping box of boxes.
Cardiac and smooth muscle don't have all three.
All three are dense regular connective tissue.
A **tendon** is a thick cord from muscle to bone.
An **aponeurosis** is a flat sheet, muscle to muscle or muscle to bone.
**Fascia** is outside the epimysium. It separates muscles and binds groups together.
